title: Post-translational modification of SPATULA by SECRET AGENT and SPINDLY promotes organ symmetry transition at the gynoecium apex
authors: Jiang Y; Curran-French S; Koh SW; Jamil I; Argirò L; Lopez S; Martins C; Saalbach G; Moubayidin L
one_liner_zh: 该文研究拟南芥转录因子SPATULA的O-糖基化修饰调控雌蕊对称性转变，虽涉及TF-DNA结合亲和力，但核心为翻译后修饰的发育功能，无AI或物理模拟方法，与课题方法轴不匹配。
abstract:
ABSTRACT

The establishment of organ symmetry during multicellular development is a fundamental process shared by most living organisms. Here, we investigated how two O -glycosyltransferases of Arabidopsis thaliana , SPINDLY (SPY) and SECRET AGENT (SEC) synergistically promote a rare bilateral-to-radial symmetry transition during patterning of the plant reproductive organ, the gynoecium. SPY and SEC modify N-terminal residues of the bHLH transcription factor SPATULA (SPT) in vivo and in vitro by attaching O -fucose and O -linked-β-N-Acetylglucosamine ( O -GlcNAc), to promote style development. This post-translational regulation does not impact SPT homo- and hetero-dimerisation events with INDEHISCENT (IND) and HECATE 1 (HEC1), although it enhances the affinity of SPT for the kinase PINOID ( PID ) gene locus to promote transcriptional repression. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism for O -GlcNAc and O -fucose post-translational decorations in controlling style development and offer the first molecular example of a synergistic role for SEC and SPY in plant post-embryonic organ patterning.
abstract_zh:
摘要

在多细胞发育过程中，器官对称性的建立是大多数生物体共有的基本过程。在此，我们研究了拟南芥（*Arabidopsis thaliana*）的两种O-糖基转移酶SPINDLY（SPY）和SECRET AGENT（SEC）如何在植物生殖器官——雌蕊（gynoecium）的形态建成中协同促进一种罕见的双侧到径向对称性转变。SPY和SEC通过将O-岩藻糖（O-fucose）和O-连接的β-N-乙酰葡糖胺（O-GlcNAc）附着到bHLH转录因子SPATULA（SPT）的N端残基上，在体内和体外修饰该因子，以促进花柱发育。这种翻译后修饰不影响SPT与INDEHISCENT（IND）和HECATE 1（HEC1）的同源及异源二聚化事件，尽管它增强了SPT对激酶PINOID（*PID*）基因位点的亲和力，以促进转录抑制。我们的发现揭示了一种先前未被识别的O-GlcNAc和O-岩藻糖翻译后修饰在控制花柱发育中的机制，并提供了SEC和SPY在植物胚后器官模式形成中协同作用的第一个分子实例。
